This provisional design conclusion helps a developer choose between the two specified JSON checkpoint mechanisms; independent review remains pending.","scope":"One single-process JSON checkpoint, one writer, an existing complete checkpoint, a distinct temporary file and no subsequent mutation. The saved outputs contain zero experiments, metrics, experiment receipts or independent grades; there are no measured results to reuse.","takeaway":"B separates preparation from publication. Successful renaming is documented as atomic in [Python os.replace](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.replace). [Linux rename(2)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/rename.2.html), DESCRIPTION, documents replacement without an interval where the destination pathname is missing. This concerns pathname visibility, not persistence after power loss. Complete-JSON publication follows conditionally from preparing complete JSON before replacement; its advantage over A is mechanism reasoning, not a measured interruption result.","walkthrough":"Concrete with/without example, explicitly unmeasured: checkpoint.json initially contains {\"step\":10}; the intended update is {\"step\":11}. Without separate publication (A), truncate checkpoint.json and write the update directly. Interruption after truncation can leave an empty file; interruption during writing can leave incomplete JSON such as {\"step\":. These are hypothetical states derived from the specified mechanism, not observed failures. With separate publication (B), write {\"step\":11} completely into a distinct checkpoint.tmp beside checkpoint.json and close it. During this preparation, the existing checkpoint remains separate. Only then call os.replace(checkpoint.tmp, checkpoint.json). Conditional on success, pathname lookup reaches the prepared file; already-open readers can retain the old file, an inference from pathname replacement semantics. Figure F1 compares the preparation paths; F2 enlarges F1's Publish component to show the publication boundary and placement constraint. Linux rename(2), ERRORS EXDEV, requires the same mounted filesystem, even when different mounts expose the same filesystem. Prefer the destination directory for the temporary file; placement alone does not guarantee success. Treat replacement errors as failures; a cross-filesystem copy fallback has no established atomic-publication guarantee here. Durability: persistence after power loss or system crash, which is unknown here. Mount: the filesystem attachment boundary relevant to Linux EXDEV.
